title: Multi-Object Tracking: IoU Association and Lifecycle

questions.question: How is IoU defined for two axis-aligned boxes?
options: Intersection area divided by union area
The number of matching corner coordinates
questions.explanation: bbox_iou computes intersection area divided by area(left)+area(right)-intersection.

questions.question: What cost does the tracker derive from an IoU value?
options: IoU itself, so larger is worse
1-IoU, while values below the threshold are incompatible
questions.explanation: The assignment maximizes compatible IoU; conceptually its minimization cost is 1-IoU and low-IoU pairs are not eligible.

questions.question: For IoU matrix [[.9,.8],[.85,.1]], which global pairing has the larger total IoU?
questions.explanation: One-to-one assignment chooses row0-column1 and row1-column0: .8+.85=1.65, larger than .9+.1.

questions.question: When does SimpleTracker create a new Track?
options: For an unmatched detection after association
When an old track is updated
questions.explanation: Detections not used by a compatible assignment receive the next positive tracker ID.

questions.question: With max_age=0, what happens after a track is absent for one frame?
options: It is removed before a later detection can reuse its ID
Its box becomes the whole image
Its ID is changed in place
questions.explanation: A track is retained only while frame-last_frame <= max_age. At the next frame with max_age=0 the old ID is stale.

questions.question: What is an ID switch in count_id_switches?
options: A ground-truth object is paired with a different tracker ID later
questions.explanation: The helper remembers each ground-truth ID's previous matched tracker ID and counts a later change.
